title: Make isolated Task MCP validation scratch executable and eliminate false rc=126 failures
objective: Fix the exact B751 infrastructure failure: validation commands running under the retained Landlock worktree currently inherit HOME/tmp on a noexec /tmp mount, so a test that compiles and executes a native ELF fails with permission denied even when the product passes. Provide a bounded per-request executable validation scratch with fail-closed cleanup and regression coverage without weakening filesystem scope or exposing credentials.
acceptance: Reproduce B751's rc=126 with a validation command that compiles a minimal C executable into inherited TMPDIR and runs it; distinguish noexec from compiler/product failure.

Give each isolated validation run a private executable scratch directory that is inside the validation sandbox's writable authority. Prefer an explicitly probed exec-capable tmpfs/path and fail closed if no safe executable scratch exists; never chmod or remount a shared filesystem.

Preserve Landlock/bubblewrap scope, shell-free validation argv parsing, provider credential isolation, isolated task DB and parent-repo immutability. The repair must not add arbitrary writable directories or leak the parent environment.

Set TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP consistently only for validation, include the scratch in the sandbox allowlist, use request-unique 0700 ownership, reject symlinks and clean it after success, failure, timeout and cancellation.

Add tests for compile+execute success, normal non-native validation, deliberate test failure propagation, timeout, cleanup, symlink rejection, no credential leakage and concurrent request isolation. Existing worker_workspace/process_launcher tests must pass.
Do not touch task queue semantics, callback routing, dashboard, model code, roadmap/STATE, commits or remote state. Stop at Codex review.
commit_contract: NO_COMMIT. Worker fixes and tests only the isolated validation executable-scratch boundary, then stops at Codex review.
